title: Uses of the infinitive (with to)
en:
Use to + infinitive:

1. After verbs like want, need, decide, hope, plan, learn, forget, promise, offer, manage, would like: I've decided to learn Spanish.

2. To say why (purpose): I went to the bank to get some money (not for get).

3. After adjectives: It's easy to understand. Nice to meet you.

4. After question words and after something / anything / somewhere: I don't know what to do. Is there anything to eat?

Negative: not to + infinitive: He promised not to be late. With want / ask / tell: She wants me to help her (not wants that I help).
ru: to + глагол: после want/need/decide/hope и др.; для цели («чтобы», не for); после прилагательных; после вопросительных слов и something/anything. Отрицание — not to. want/ask/tell + кого-то + to.

qs.q: I've decided ___ a new car.
She promised ___ late again.
I went to the shop ___ (buy) some milk.
It's important ___ (drink) enough water.
Would you like ___ (come) to dinner on Saturday?
I don't know what ___.
Is there anything ___ in the fridge?
Correct the mistake: “I'm learning English for get a better job.”
a: I'm learning English to get a better job.
I am learning English to get a better job.
I'm learning English in order to get a better job.
I am learning English in order to get a better job.

qs.q: Correct the mistake: “She wants that I help her.”
a: She wants me to help her.

qs.q: Correct the mistake: “It's easy understand this rule.”
a: It's easy to understand this rule.
It is easy to understand this rule.

qs.q: Put the words in the correct order.
qs.a: i forgot to send you the report

qs.q: Put the words in the correct order.
qs.a: can you tell me where to park

qs.q: In “I came here to learn English”, “to learn” explains why I came.
After “would like” we use the -ing form: “I'd like going home.”
qs.exp: would like + to: I'd like to go home.

qs.q: We hope ___ you again soon.
I need somewhere ___ tonight.
I'm sorry ___ (hear) that you're ill.
My manager asked me ___ (not / be) late.
Did you manage ___ the tickets?
They're saving money ___ a house.
